story-food.title: Traditional Food of Himachal Pradesh — Top 8 Must-Try Himachali Dishes

blocks.text: Traditional Food of Himachal Pradesh 🍽️
Himachali cuisine is a rich tapestry of flavors shaped by mountain climate, seasonal produce, and centuries of tradition. Simple yet deeply satisfying — the food of Devbhoomi is a journey in itself.
🫓 Aktori
Traditional festive cake made from buckwheat/rice flour — Himachal’s celebrations are incomplete without Aktori.
🍲 Madra
Chicken peas with yogurt, spiced with cardamom and cloves — a staple of Himachali Dham served at weddings and festivals.
🍱 Dhaam
The royal feast of HP — served on leaf plates (pattals) with Madra, rice, dal, and chutneys. A cultural institution.
🫓 Babru
The Himachali Poori — stuffed with black gram (urad dal). Popular breakfast dish served with tamarind chutney.
🥔 Palda Aloo
Quick Pahari-style potato curry with curd — simple, nutritious, and a staple of Himachali home cooking.
🎃 Kadoo Auriya
Famous Himachali pumpkin dish served with Kulcha and Tadka dal — simple, flavorful, deeply Himachali.
🍚 Tudkiya Bhath
HP’s delectable pulao with mashed dal and lime juice — a complete and satisfying mountain meal.
🐟 Kullu Trout
Fresh river trout with minimal spices — a nutritious delicacy from pristine Himachali mountain streams.

story-dance.title: हिमाचल प्रदेश के प्रमुख लोक नृत्य — Folk Dances of Himachal Pradesh

blocks.text: हिमाचल प्रदेश के प्रमुख लोक नृत्य
Himachal Pradesh is a treasure trove of vibrant folk dances, each telling a unique story of our mountains, seasons, and traditions — the heartbeat of Himachali culture.
🎭 नाटी (Nati)

The most popular folk dance of Himachal Pradesh — holds the Guinness World Record for the largest folk dance. Performed in circles by groups in traditional Himachali attire during festivals and harvests across Kullu, Sirmaur, and Shimla.
🎵 बकायंग नृत्य (Bakayag Dance)
A traditional group dance performed at temple grounds and cultural fairs — celebrating community and devotion through rhythmic circular movement.
🪘 छनक छाम (Chanak Chham)
A masked Buddhist dance from Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur — performed by monks at monasteries during religious festivals, featuring elaborate masks and colorful costumes depicting Buddhist mythology.
💃 कयांग नृत्य (Kayag Dance)
A traditional circular dance from tribal areas — performed by men and women holding hands, representing the unity and harmony of mountain communities.
🌄 Dangi Dance
Traditional folk dance of the Dangi tribal community — characterized by energetic movements and colorful attire during harvest festivals.

story-parmar.title: Yashwant Singh Parmar — Father of Himachal Pradesh (1963–1977)

blocks.text: Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar — The Architect of Modern Himachal Pradesh

Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar (1906–1981) is revered as the Father of Himachal Pradesh — the visionary leader who brought the hill districts of northern India together to form the state of Himachal Pradesh on 25 January 1971 .
🏔️ The Making of Himachal Pradesh

When India gained independence in 1947, Parmar played a pivotal role in merging 30 small princely hill states of Punjab Hills into Himachal Pradesh — first as a Chief Commissioner’s Province on 15 April 1948 , then as a Part C State, and finally as a full-fledged state on 25 January 1971 .
🌿 Legacy & Contributions
Land Reforms — abolished feudal zamindari system; gave land to the tillers
Education — established schools across remote mountain areas
Horticulture — pioneered apple cultivation, transforming HP’s economy
Road Connectivity — connected remote Himalayan villages for the first time
Women Empowerment — championed women’s education in hill communities
World Himachali Organization draws inspiration from Dr. Parmar’s vision of a united, progressive Himachal Pradesh. His legacy guides our mission of देवभूमि सेवायै .
